facts.statement: The dinosaur was named after Muttaburra, the location in Queensland, Australia where its fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: It was named after Muttaburra, the site in Queensland, Australia, where it was found.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus is the second most completely known non-avian dinosaur from Australia, following Kunbarrasaurus.
facts.quote: After Kunbarrasaurus, it is Australia's most completely known dinosaur from skeletal remains.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus was chosen from twelve candidates to serve as the official fossil emblem of the State of Queensland.
facts.quote: The dinosaur was selected from twelve candidates to become the official fossil emblem of the State of Queensland.

facts.statement: The species was formally named in 1981 by Bartholomai and Ralph Molnar, giving it the specific name langdoni to honor its discoverer.
facts.quote: it was named in 1981 by Bartholomai and Ralph Molnar, who honoured its discoverer with its specific name, langdoni.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus lived during the middle Cretaceous period, approximately 112 to 98.6 million years ago, in the Albian and Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 112 a 98,6 millones de años, en el Albiense y Cenomaniense

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus was approximately 8 meters long with initial body mass estimates around 2.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Muttaburrasaurus was about 8 m, with initial body mass estimates of around 2.8 MT.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus is comparable in size to large T. rex specimens and bull African bush elephants, making it the largest ornithischian known to retain premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: This would make Muttaburrasaurus comparable in size to some of the larger specimens of T. rex and bull African bush elephants, making it by far the largest ornithischian to retain premaxillary teeth.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype specimen measures 1015 mm in length.
facts.quote: The femur of the holotype has a length of 1015 mm.

facts.statement: The skull of Muttaburrasaurus was long with a triangular cross-section when viewed from above.
facts.quote: The skull of Muttaburrasaurus was rather long, with a triangular cross-section when seen from above.

facts.statement: The snout features a strongly enlarged hollow bulge that was originally thought to be a resonating chamber for calls or visual display.
facts.quote: The snout includes a strongly enlarged, hollow bulge originally considered to have been a resonating chamber to produce that might distinctive calls or a visual display features.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus is unique among large ornithischians for retaining premaxillary teeth, a trait usually lost in derived members of the group.
facts.quote: Muttaburrasaurus is unique amongst ornithischians of its size class for possessing premaxillary teeth, a feature that is ancestral to all ornithischians and is present in many small or basal species, but are usually lost in nearly all the large or derived members of the group.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Muttaburrasaurus was capable of quadrupedal movement, though recent studies suggest it adopted a bipedal posture similar to rhabdodonts.
facts.quote: Whether Muttaburrasaurus is capable of quadrupedal movement has been debated; was originally thought to be an "iguanodontid", though recent studies indicate a rhabdodont position which generally adopted a bipedal posture.

facts.statement: Quadrupedal locomotion in Muttaburrasaurus likely occurred only when moving slowly or while stationary to browse on foliage.
facts.quote: Quadrupedal locomotion would appear to be reserved for when the animal was moving slowly or when stationary and browsing on foliage.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus possessed very powerful jaws equipped with shearing teeth.
facts.quote: Muttaburrasaurus had very powerful jaws equipped with shearing teeth.

facts.statement: In Muttaburrasaurus, replacement teeth grew directly under the functional teeth with only a single erupted generation, precluding a chewing motion.
facts.quote: in Muttaburrasaurus, they grew directly under them, and only a single erupted generation was present, thus precluding a chewing motion.

facts.statement: In 1981, Molnar speculated that Muttaburrasaurus had an omnivorous diet and occasionally ate carrion based on its dental qualities.
facts.quote: In 1981, Molnar speculated that these qualities indicated an omnivorous diet, implying that Muttaburrasaurus occasionally ate carrion.

facts.statement: A 2026 reanalysis suggests Muttaburrasaurus was a selective feeder with a strong sense of smell due to its narrow snout.
facts.quote: Reanalysis of the holotype skull published in 2026 suggests that Muttaburrasaurus was a selective feeder due to its narrow snout and possessed a strong sense of smell.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus has been classified in various analyses as a member of Rhabdodontomorpha, but recent research suggests it may belong to the basal clade Elasmaria.
facts.quote: It has been recovered in some analyses as a member of the iguanodontian clade Rhabdodontomorpha, but more recent research has suggested a more basal position in the ornithopod family tree, potentially as a member of Elasmaria.

facts.statement: Molnar originally assigned Muttaburrasaurus to Iguanodontidae, but later authors suggested it belonged to basal groups like Camptosauridae, Dryosauridae, or Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Molnar originally assigned Muttaburrasaurus to the Iguanodontidae. Later authors suggested more basal euornithopod groups such as the Camptosauridae, Dryosauridae, or Hypsilophodontidae.

facts.statement: Studies by Andrew McDonald indicate that Muttaburrasaurus belongs to the Rhabdodontidae.
facts.quote: Studies by Andrew McDonald indicate a position in the Rhabdodontidae.

facts.statement: In 2024, Fonseca and colleagues classified Muttaburrasaurus outside Rhabdodontomorpha as a member of the Gondwanan clade Elasmaria.
facts.quote: However, in 2024, Fonseca and colleagues considered Muttaburrasaurus to be outside Rhabdodontomorpha and instead classified it as a member of the Gondwanan clade Elasmaria, alongside Fostoria dhimbangunmal.

facts.statement: A 2026 skull redescription suggests Muttaburrasaurus is likely not a rhabdodontomorph and may fall outside the Iguanodontia clade due to features like retained premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: In their 2026 redescription of the Muttaburrasaurus skull, Herne and colleagues comment that several cranial features, including the retention of premaxillary teeth, mean the taxa is likely not a rhabdodontomorph and may even fall outside of the greater Iguanodontia clade.

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus is classified within the unranked family Rhabdodontomorpha.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Rhabdodontomorpha

facts.statement: Muttaburrasaurus is classified as a rabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaur.
facts.quote: de dinosaurio ornitópodo rabdodontomorfo

facts.statement: The holotype specimen QM F6140 was discovered in the Mackunda Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, specimen QM F6140, was found in the Mackunda Formation.

facts.statement: The "Dunluce Skull" (specimen QM F14921) was discovered in 1987 by John Stewart-Moore and 14-year-old Robert Walker on Dunluce Station.
facts.quote: A skull, known as the "Dunluce Skull", specimen QM F14921, was discovered by John Stewart-Moore and 14-year-old Robert Walker on Dunluce Station, between Hughenden and Richmond in 1987.

facts.statement: Reconstructed skeleton casts of Muttaburrasaurus, sponsored by Kellogg Company, are displayed at museums including the Queensland Museum, Flinders Discovery Centre, and the Australian Museum.
facts.quote: Reconstructed skeleton casts of Muttaburrasaurus, sponsored by Kellogg Company, have been put on display at a number of museums, including the Queensland Museum, Flinders Discovery Centre, and the Australian Museum.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the hollow bulge on the snout was a resonating chamber, with later research concluding it was part of an elongated premaxilla.
facts.quote: However, later research concluded the bulge was part of a greatly elongated premaxilla, unlikely to have played a role as a resonating chamber.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Muttaburrasaurus was an omnivore that ate carrion, a hypothesis proposed by Molnar in 1981 but later revised.
facts.quote: In 1981, Molnar speculated that these qualities indicated an omnivorous diet, implying that Muttaburrasaurus occasionally ate carrion.
